newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Super League executive director Ian Frykberg claimed the Australian Rugby League clubs are still far from reaching peace, as the ARL has stalled on its decision regarding a freeze on player signings. The initiative was conceived by ARL chief exeutive Neil Whittaker and accepted by Super League clubs on Wednesday. Page 20.

In response to the Collingwood Magpies rapidly declining position on the Australian Football League ladder from first to 11th, five players were dropped from the first grade side last night including Anthony Rocca, Richard Osborne and Stephen Patterson. Pge 20.

Despite bad weather Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor defeated Olympic champion Marie-Jose Perec at the Lausanne Grand Prix yesterday in the 200 metres event. The win boosts Gainsford-Taylor's hopes to win a medal at the upcoming championships in Athens. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Under-20 women's basketball coach Ray Tomlinson will be forced to distribute court time equally amongst his 12 player team at the world championships which start this weekend in Natal, Brazil. Page 45.

The Australian Football League is looking to establish a second team in Sydney and may relocate one of its Melbourne-based teams rather than expand its 16-team format. The expansion to Sydney will allow the AFL to maximise use of the Olympic Stadium folloing the 2000 Olympics. Page 44.

New Zealand rugby union coach John Hart believes Australian and New Zealand rugby teams could be subject to a slide down the international ladder because of player burnout. There are also concerns that representative games are no longer memorable and have become meaningless. Page 45.
THE AGE

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor decided to bat after winning a toss he would have preferred to lose at the third Test which began in Manchester, England yesterday. Taylor decided to bat knowing that no team has ever won at Manchester after sending the opposition in. Page D5.

The Australian women's water polo team defeated European champions Italy 8-5 yesterday at the World Cup in Nancy, France. The win secures a semi-final placing for the team following their opening win against Canada. Page D13.

Ballart horse trainer Robert Smerdon should be reasonably confident of a second win at the Grand National Hurdle at Flemington tomorrow with Highland Bill, but would be wary of the chances of New Zealand horse Richard Cranium, who is the betting favourite Page D12.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian soccer coach Terry Venables said it would be foolish and suicidal to underestimate their opponent, the New Zealand All Whites, in tomorrow's World Cup qualifier. Venables believes that the All Whites will still be hurting from the Australian team's 3-0 victory last weekend in Auckland. Page 98.

Australian cyclist Robbie McEwen may join team-mate Pat Jonker in the Tour de France and give Australia a record five starters. McEwen is recovering from a crash in May at the Tour of Durkirk were he needed a plate inserted in his shoulder and fluid drained from his knee. Page 99.

Carlton Australian Football League player Stephen Silvagni will be given until tomorrow to prove his fitness for Carlton's match of the round against the Western Bulldogs. In other team news, Collingwood has rushed back Tony Francis, who has only played two games this season because of a serious ankle injury. Page 110.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton last night refused to confirm reports that he has been appointed as chairman of the New South Wales TAB board to guide the TAB past privatisation. The NSW TAB is to be privatised early next year and Pemberton is the favourite for the chair's position. Page 118.

According to the Wisden cricket ratings, Australia will remain the world's best Test nation even if England were to beat the team in the present Ashes series. Australia leads the ratings followed by the West Indies, South Africa, India, Pakistan and Englad. Page 117.

Former Australian wrestling champion Larry O'Dea passed away on Monday aged 53. O'Dea began his career at the age of 16 and achieved popularity in the 1960s and 70s as a star on Channel 9's World Championship Wrestling. Page 109.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
